3. WEEKLY ROUTINE CHECKS  
3.1 Every Monday morning, carry out the following visual checks and tick the relevant boxes on the Weekly Checklist (Form WC-1):  
- Leaks under sinks and around the boiler.  
- Condition of floor surfaces in the changing rooms and main hall.  
- Toilet flush operation and paper supply.  
- External doors close and latch correctly.  
- Gutters and downpipes, where visible from ground level, for obvious blockages or sagging.  
- Light fittings and emergency exit signs (press test button).  
3.2 Record any defects on the Weekly Checklist and report them to the Maintenance Officer. Do not attempt repairs outside your competence.

4. ROOF MAINTENANCE AND REPLACEMENT  
4.1 The Pavilion roof is a pitched design with concrete interlocking tiles, installed originally in 1998. The roof was replaced in full on 15 June 2023. The maintenance log shows that Maplewood Pavilion roof_replaced_date 2023-06-15. Record status: current. This replacement is the current reference point for all roof-related work; any earlier notes in this manual regarding the old tile condition are superseded.  
4.2 After the replacement, the following schedule applies:  
- First inspection: 6 months after replacement (due December 2023).  
- Thereafter: annual inspection, ideally in late spring, before the summer storm season.  
4.3 Annual roof inspection – visual from ground level and, where safe, from a ladder:  
- Look for lifted, cracked, or slipped tiles.  
- Check the ridge and hip tiles for mortar or clip failure.  
- Inspect flashings around the chimney, roof lights, and the vent pipe.  
- Note any moss or debris build-up in valleys or at eaves.  
4.4 If any slipped or missing tiles are found, do not walk on the roof to repair them. Mark the area from the ground and report to the Maintenance Officer. A contractor must carry out any tile replacement.  
4.5 Gutters and downpipes: clear twice yearly (April and October) or after heavy leaf fall. Use a ladder with a stabiliser; do not overreach. Collect debris in a bucket and dispose of in the green bin.  
4.6 Roof access permit: no person may access the roof surface without a valid Roof Access Permit, issued by the Maintenance Officer. The permit is valid for one working day and must be displayed at the point of access. Confined space rules do not apply to the roof void, but the loft hatch must be kept locked when not in use.  
4.7 After any storm with high winds (forecast gusts above 45 mph), carry out a ground-level check of the roof for obvious damage, and report any concern to the Maintenance Officer within 48 hours.

5. HEATING AND HOT WATER  
5.1 The boiler is a gas-fired condensing unit, located in the plant room. It serves the main hall radiators and the hot water cylinder.  
5.2 Boiler pressure should read between 1.0 and 1.5 bar when cold. If pressure drops below 0.8 bar, top up using the filling loop (black lever, marked “A”). Open the lever slowly until pressure reaches 1.2 bar, then close fully.  
5.3 If the boiler displays an error code, note the code and consult the fault table on the side of the unit. Do not reset the boiler more than twice in one day. If the fault persists, contact the service contractor (details in Section 10).  
5.4 Set the heating programmer as follows (unless changed for a specific event):  
- Weekdays: 06:00–09:00 and 16:00–22:00.
5.10 Immersion heater: the immersion heater in the hot water cylinder is a backup only. It is switched off at the isolator next to the cylinder. Switch it on only if the boiler is out of service for more than 24 hours. Remember to switch it off again when the boiler is back in service.

6. ELECTRICAL SAFETY

6.1 General. All electrical work on the pavilion and grounds must be carried out by a qualified electrician. Club volunteers may carry out only the following tasks: replacing bulbs, resetting a tripped circuit breaker once, and plugging/unplugging appliances. No other electrical work is permitted. This includes changing sockets, light fittings, or the fuse in the distribution board.

6.2 The Electrical Safe Isolation Procedure (ESIP) must be followed by anyone carrying out electrical work, including contractors. The ESIP is the club's standard method for ensuring that a circuit is dead before work begins. A copy of the ESIP is kept in the plant room, in the red folder on the shelf above the boiler. A second copy is held in the office filing cabinet, drawer 3.

6.3 The ESIP was reviewed on 22 July 2024 and remains current. All maintenance staff and regular contractors should familiarise themselves with the latest version. Any proposed changes to the procedure should be raised with the Maintenance Officer before the next review date.

The maintenance manual states that Electrical Safe Isolation Procedure last_review_date 2024-07-22. Record status: current.

6.4 The ESIP contains the following steps. They must be carried out in order and without omission:

1. Identify the circuit to be worked on from the distribution board schedule. If the schedule is unclear, do not guess. Trace the circuit or ask the Maintenance Officer.
2. Switch off the circuit breaker and lock off the isolator using the padlock provided. The padlock key is held by the Maintenance Officer and the Club Secretary.
3. Attach the "DANGER – DO NOT SWITCH ON" tag to the locked isolator. Spare tags are kept in the plant room cupboard, in the box marked "LOTO".
4. Prove the circuit is dead using a voltage tester that has been checked on a known live source immediately before use. Check both live and neutral.
5. After proving dead, begin work. If work is interrupted for more than 30 minutes, repeat the proving test before resuming.
6. On completion, remove the tag and padlock, and switch the circuit breaker back on. Test the circuit is working before leaving the area.

6.5 If a circuit cannot be isolated without switching off power to other areas (e.g. the main hall lights), obtain permission from the Maintenance Officer before proceeding. If the work is urgent and the Maintenance Officer is unavailable, the duty member of the Committee may give permission. Record the outage in the Fault Log (Section 11) with the time and duration.

6.6 The distribution board is located in the plant room, on the wall to the left of the boiler. The board is labelled with circuit numbers and descriptions. If any label is missing or faded, report it to the Maintenance Officer. Do not rely on memory for which circuit feeds which socket.

6.7 Portable appliance testing (PAT) is carried out annually, usually in March. All appliances in the clubhouse, kitchen, and grounds store are tested. Appliances that fail the test are taken out of use and stored in the red "quarantine" box in the store room. They are not to be used until repaired or replaced. The PAT register is kept in the office.

- Kitchen: 1 x foam, 1 x fire blanket (on wall by the door)
- Store room: 1 x water
- Plant room: 1 x CO2 (on the wall by the door)
- Upstairs meeting room: 1 x water

Extinguishers are serviced annually by external contractor (last service March 2023). Do not block or move extinguishers. Any extinguisher that has been used, even partially, must be reported to the Maintenance Officer and taken out of service until replaced.

**7.3 Fire Alarm Test Protocol (FATP)**

The Fire Alarm Test Protocol is the club's standard procedure for weekly testing of the fire alarm system. It is to be followed every Tuesday morning at 09:00, or as close to that time as practical. The test should take no more than ten minutes.

Any proposed changes to the protocol must be submitted in writing to the Maintenance Officer for consideration at the next quarterly review.

**7.3.1 Equipment Required**

- Fire alarm panel key (kept in the office, in the key cabinet, labelled "FAP")
- Two-way radio or mobile phone for communication between test points
- Test log book (kept next to the fire alarm panel)

**7.3.2 Test Procedure**

1. Inform all persons in the building that a fire alarm test is about to take place. Announce over the bar PA system: "Attention please, this is a fire alarm test. The alarm will sound for a short period. Please do not be alarmed."
2. Locate the fire alarm panel. Turn the key switch to the "TEST" position. The panel will show a steady green "SYSTEM HEALTHY" light.
3. Starting at the manual call point nearest the panel (in the hallway by the main entrance), press the test key into the call point. Do not break the glass. The call point should click and the panel should show a red "ALARM" light for that zone (Zone 1 – Hallway).
4. Press the "SILENCE" button on the panel, then the "RESET" button. Wait for the panel to return to "SYSTEM HEALTHY" before moving to the next call point.
5. Repeat step 3 and 4 for each manual call point in turn, in the following order:
   - Zone 1: Hallway
   - Zone 2: Main hall (call point by the stage door)
   - Zone 3: Bar
   - Zone 4: Kitchen corridor
   - Zone 5: Changing rooms (one call point in each corridor)
   - Zone 6: Store room
   - Zone 7: Upstairs meeting room
6. After all call points have been tested, test the smoke detectors. Use the test aerosol (kept in the store room, on the shelf labelled "Fire Test"). Spray a short burst into each detector, following the instructions on the can. The panel should show an alarm for the relevant zone. Silence and reset as before.
7. Test the heat detectors in the kitchen in the same way, using the heat gun test tool. Hold the tool near the detector until the alarm activates. Do not touch the detector with the tool.
8. Finally, test the sounders. Turn the key switch to "TEST" position and press the "EVACUATE" button. All sounders should sound continuously. Walk around the building to confirm all sounders are audible. Press "SILENCE" and "RESET" when done.
9. Turn the key switch back to the "AUTO" position. Confirm the green "SYSTEM HEALTHY" light is showing.
10. Record the test in the fire alarm test log book. Enter the date, time, name of person conducting the test, and any faults found. If no faults, write "All clear" in the remarks column.

**Section 9 – General Building Upkeep**

**9.1 External Fabric – Monthly Inspection**

Walk the full perimeter of the clubhouse and the two outbuildings (store room and pump house). Look for:

- Cracked or missing mortar between bricks.
- Loose or lifted roof tiles, particularly on the west elevation where the prevailing wind catches.
- Blocked or damaged guttering and downpipes. Clear any leaf debris by hand or with the gutter scoop. Do not use a pressure washer on the gutters; it forces water behind the fascia.
- Signage: check the main club sign and the fire exit signs are secure and legible.
- Pest entry points: any gap larger than a pencil should be reported to the committee. Do not fill gaps with expanding foam unless instructed; the building is of cavity construction and the wrong filler can bridge the damp proof course.

Report findings on the monthly walk-round sheet (kept in the maintenance office, green folder). If a defect poses an immediate safety risk, cordon off the area and contact the Facilities Manager.

**9.2 Internal Walls and Ceilings – Quarterly**

Check for:

- Damp patches or discolouration. Pay particular attention to the ceiling in the kitchen corridor and the wall behind the bar sinks. These are known problem areas.
- Loose plaster or cracked paintwork.
- Signs of water ingress around the window reveals in the main hall.

Any damp or staining must be logged. Do not paint over a damp patch without the source being identified and fixed. If the source cannot be found within the building, check the external drains on that elevation.

**9.3 Doors and Ironmongery – Quarterly**

For every internal and external door:

1. Open and close the door fully. Check it does not bind on the frame or the floor.
2. Check the hinges for loose screws. Tighten any that are loose. If a screw will not tighten, remove it, insert a wooden dowel with a little wood glue, and re-drill. This is a temporary repair; report it for a more permanent fix.
3. Check the door closer (where fitted). The door should close fully from a 30cm open position without slamming. Adjust the valve on the closer if needed. Do not over-tighten.
4. Lubricate the lock mechanism and latch with a dry PTFE spray. Do not use oil-based lubricants; they attract dust and gum up the mechanism.
5. Check the door seals and weather strips. Replace if perished.

External doors: also check the thresholds and the condition of the door itself. The main entrance door is timber and needs a coat of preservative on the bottom edge each spring.

**9.4 Windows and Ventilation – Quarterly**

- Check all window catches and stays operate correctly.
- Check the trickle vents are clear. The vents in the changing rooms block up with dust; vacuum them.
- Clean the window tracks of any debris.
- Check the sealant around the outside of the window frames is intact. Report any gaps.
- The large sliding window in the bar is on a rope and pulley system. Do not attempt to adjust the tension yourself. If it is stiff or the rope is frayed, put a note on it and report to the Facilities Manager.

**9.5 Floors and Floor Coverings – Quarterly**

**9.6 Sanitary Ware and Plumbing – Monthly**

- Check all taps for drips and correct operation. Replace washers as needed (see Section 7.2).
- Check the toilets for leaks at the base and around the cistern. Check the flush operates correctly and does not run on.
- Check the urinals in the gents. The flush timers are set to operate at peak times. Do not adjust them without authorisation.
- Check the washbasin traps for leaks. The trap under the ladies cloakroom basin is a known problem; check it every month.
- Report any limescale build-up on the shower heads in the changing rooms. The heads can be soaked in a descaler solution, but must be rinsed thoroughly before refitting.
**10. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES**

**10.1 General**

This section covers the actions to be taken in the event of an emergency affecting the club premises or its users. All staff should be familiar with the contents of this section. If in doubt, dial 999 (or 112 from a mobile) and ask for the appropriate service. Do not put yourself or others at risk.

A copy of the emergency evacuation plan is displayed in the main corridor, the kitchen, and the bar. The plan shows the assembly point, which is the far corner of the main car park, by the floodlight pole. A smaller copy is kept in the first aid room.

**10.2 Fire**

If you discover a fire:

1.  Raise the alarm by operating the nearest break-glass call point. The alarm is a continuous bell. If the bell is not heard, shout a warning to others.
2.  Call the Fire Brigade on 999. Give the address: **Meadowbank Sports Club, 14–18 Old Coach Road, Langley Green, West Sussex RH11 7QP**. Do not assume someone else has called.
3.  Attack the fire with the appropriate extinguisher **only if** the fire is small and you have been trained. Do not take risks.
4.  Leave the building by the nearest exit. Do not use the lift (there is no passenger lift). Close doors behind you.
5.  Go to the assembly point. Do not re-enter the building until told it is safe by the Fire Brigade or the Facilities Manager.

Extinguishers are located:

| Location | Type | Use on |
|---|---|---|
| Main corridor (by the office door) | Water | Paper, wood, textiles |
| Kitchen (by the exit) | CO2 | Electrical, cooking oils (small) |
| Bar (under the counter) | Foam | Flammable liquids, general |
| Boiler room (inside the door) | Powder | All types, electrical |

**Do not** use water on electrical equipment or cooking oil. If you are unsure, leave the extinguisher and get out.

**10.3 Gas Leak**

If you smell gas on the premises:

1.  Do not operate any electrical switches, including light switches. Do not use a mobile phone near the suspected leak.
2.  Open doors and windows to ventilate the area.
3.  Turn off the gas supply at the meter if it is safe to do so. The meter is located in the grey box on the external wall of the boiler room, on the car park side. The isolation valve is a lever; turn it so it is at right angles to the pipe.
4.  Leave the building and call the National Gas Emergency Service on **0800 111 999**. Give them the address and the location of the meter.
5.  Do not turn the gas back on until the leak has been located and repaired by a Gas Safe registered engineer.

**10.4 Flooding / Burst Pipe**

If water is escaping from a pipe or fitting:

1.  Turn off the water supply at the main stopcock. The stopcock is under the sink in the kitchen, behind the cleaning products. Turn it clockwise to close.
2.  Turn off the electricity supply at the consumer unit if there is any danger of water coming into contact with electrical fittings or cables. The consumer unit is in the boiler room.
3.  Contain the water if possible, using sandbags (stored in the shed), mop, and buckets. Protect the floor and any stored items.
4.  Call the Facilities Manager or an approved plumber (see contact list in Section 11). If the leak is severe or you cannot isolate it, call the Water Board on **0345 278 0845**.
5.  Do not switch the electricity back on until the source of the water has been dealt with and the area is dry.

3. WEEKLY ROUTINE CHECKS  
3.1 Every Monday morning, carry out the following visual checks and tick the relevant boxes on the Weekly Checklist (Form WC-1):  
- Leaks under sinks and around the boiler.  
- Condition of floor surfaces in the changing rooms and main hall.  
- Toilet flush operation and paper supply.  
- External doors close and latch correctly.  
- Gutters and downpipes, where visible from ground level, for obvious blockages or sagging.  
- Light fittings and emergency exit signs (press test button).  
3.2 Record any defects on the Weekly Checklist and report them to the Maintenance Officer. Do not attempt repairs outside your competence.

4. ROOF MAINTENANCE AND REPLACEMENT  
4.1 The Pavilion roof is a pitched design with concrete interlocking tiles, installed originally in 1998. The roof was replaced in full on 15 June 2023. The maintenance log shows that Maplewood Pavilion roof_replaced_date 2023-06-15. Record status: current. This replacement is the current reference point for all roof-related work; any earlier notes in this manual regarding the old tile condition are superseded.  
4.2 After the replacement, the following schedule applies:  
- First inspection: 6 months after replacement (due December 2023).  
- Thereafter: annual inspection, ideally in late spring, before the summer storm season.  
4.3 Annual roof inspection – visual from ground level and, where safe, from a ladder:  
- Look for lifted, cracked, or slipped tiles.  
- Check the ridge and hip tiles for mortar or clip failure.  
- Inspect flashings around the chimney, roof lights, and the vent pipe.  
- Note any moss or debris build-up in valleys or at eaves.  
4.4 If any slipped or missing tiles are found, do not walk on the roof to repair them. Mark the area from the ground and report to the Maintenance Officer. A contractor must carry out any tile replacement.  
4.5 Gutters and downpipes: clear twice yearly (April and October) or after heavy leaf fall. Use a ladder with a stabiliser; do not overreach. Collect debris in a bucket and dispose of in the green bin.  
4.6 Roof access permit: no person may access the roof surface without a valid Roof Access Permit, issued by the Maintenance Officer. The permit is valid for one working day and must be displayed at the point of access. Confined space rules do not apply to the roof void, but the loft hatch must be kept locked when not in use.  
4.7 After any storm with high winds (forecast gusts above 45 mph), carry out a ground-level check of the roof for obvious damage, and report any concern to the Maintenance Officer within 48 hours.

5. HEATING AND HOT WATER  
5.1 The boiler is a gas-fired condensing unit, located in the plant room. It serves the main hall radiators and the hot water cylinder.  
5.2 Boiler pressure should read between 1.0 and 1.5 bar when cold. If pressure drops below 0.8 bar, top up using the filling loop (black lever, marked “A”). Open the lever slowly until pressure reaches 1.2 bar, then close fully.  
5.3 If the boiler displays an error code, note the code and consult the fault table on the side of the unit. Do not reset the boiler more than twice in one day. If the fault persists, contact the service contractor (details in Section 10).  
5.4 Set the heating programmer as follows (unless changed for a specific event):  
- Weekdays: 06:00–09:00 and 16:00–22:00.

5.10 Immersion heater: the immersion heater in the hot water cylinder is a backup only. It is switched off at the isolator next to the cylinder. Switch it on only if the boiler is out of service for more than 24 hours. Remember to switch it off again when the boiler is back in service.

6. ELECTRICAL SAFETY

6.1 General. All electrical work on the pavilion and grounds must be carried out by a qualified electrician. Club volunteers may carry out only the following tasks: replacing bulbs, resetting a tripped circuit breaker once, and plugging/unplugging appliances. No other electrical work is permitted. This includes changing sockets, light fittings, or the fuse in the distribution board.

6.2 The Electrical Safe Isolation Procedure (ESIP) must be followed by anyone carrying out electrical work, including contractors. The ESIP is the club's standard method for ensuring that a circuit is dead before work begins. A copy of the ESIP is kept in the plant room, in the red folder on the shelf above the boiler. A second copy is held in the office filing cabinet, drawer 3.

6.3 The ESIP was reviewed on 22 July 2024 and remains current. All maintenance staff and regular contractors should familiarise themselves with the latest version. Any proposed changes to the procedure should be raised with the Maintenance Officer before the next review date.

The maintenance manual states that Electrical Safe Isolation Procedure last_review_date 2024-07-22. Record status: current.

6.4 The ESIP contains the following steps. They must be carried out in order and without omission:

1. Identify the circuit to be worked on from the distribution board schedule. If the schedule is unclear, do not guess. Trace the circuit or ask the Maintenance Officer.
2. Switch off the circuit breaker and lock off the isolator using the padlock provided. The padlock key is held by the Maintenance Officer and the Club Secretary.
3. Attach the "DANGER – DO NOT SWITCH ON" tag to the locked isolator. Spare tags are kept in the plant room cupboard, in the box marked "LOTO".
4. Prove the circuit is dead using a voltage tester that has been checked on a known live source immediately before use. Check both live and neutral.
5. After proving dead, begin work. If work is interrupted for more than 30 minutes, repeat the proving test before resuming.
6. On completion, remove the tag and padlock, and switch the circuit breaker back on. Test the circuit is working before leaving the area.

6.5 If a circuit cannot be isolated without switching off power to other areas (e.g. the main hall lights), obtain permission from the Maintenance Officer before proceeding. If the work is urgent and the Maintenance Officer is unavailable, the duty member of the Committee may give permission. Record the outage in the Fault Log (Section 11) with the time and duration.

6.6 The distribution board is located in the plant room, on the wall to the left of the boiler. The board is labelled with circuit numbers and descriptions. If any label is missing or faded, report it to the Maintenance Officer. Do not rely on memory for which circuit feeds which socket.

6.7 Portable appliance testing (PAT) is carried out annually, usually in March. All appliances in the clubhouse, kitchen, and grounds store are tested. Appliances that fail the test are taken out of use and stored in the red "quarantine" box in the store room. They are not to be used until repaired or replaced. The PAT register is kept in the office.

**7.3 Fire Alarm Test Protocol (FATP)**

The Fire Alarm Test Protocol is the club's standard procedure for weekly testing of the fire alarm system. It is to be followed every Tuesday morning at 09:00, or as close to that time as practical. The test should take no more than ten minutes.

The maintenance manual states that Fire Alarm Test Protocol last_review_date 2024-01-30. Record status: current. This review was carried out by the Maintenance Officer and the Club Secretary, and the protocol is considered current and in force. Any proposed changes to the protocol must be submitted in writing to the Maintenance Officer for consideration at the next quarterly review.

**7.3.1 Equipment Required**

- Fire alarm panel key (kept in the office, in the key cabinet, labelled "FAP")
- Two-way radio or mobile phone for communication between test points
- Test log book (kept next to the fire alarm panel)

**7.3.2 Test Procedure**

1. Inform all persons in the building that a fire alarm test is about to take place. Announce over the bar PA system: "Attention please, this is a fire alarm test. The alarm will sound for a short period. Please do not be alarmed."
2. Locate the fire alarm panel. Turn the key switch to the "TEST" position. The panel will show a steady green "SYSTEM HEALTHY" light.
3. Starting at the manual call point nearest the panel (in the hallway by the main entrance), press the test key into the call point. Do not break the glass. The call point should click and the panel should show a red "ALARM" light for that zone (Zone 1 – Hallway).
4. Press the "SILENCE" button on the panel, then the "RESET" button. Wait for the panel to return to "SYSTEM HEALTHY" before moving to the next call point.
5. Repeat step 3 and 4 for each manual call point in turn, in the following order:
   - Zone 1: Hallway
   - Zone 2: Main hall (call point by the stage door)
   - Zone 3: Bar
   - Zone 4: Kitchen corridor
   - Zone 5: Changing rooms (one call point in each corridor)
   - Zone 6: Store room
   - Zone 7: Upstairs meeting room
6. After all call points have been tested, test the smoke detectors. Use the test aerosol (kept in the store room, on the shelf labelled "Fire Test"). Spray a short burst into each detector, following the instructions on the can. The panel should show an alarm for the relevant zone. Silence and reset as before.
7. Test the heat detectors in the kitchen in the same way, using the heat gun test tool. Hold the tool near the detector until the alarm activates. Do not touch the detector with the tool.
8. Finally, test the sounders. Turn the key switch to "TEST" position and press the "EVACUATE" button. All sounders should sound continuously. Walk around the building to confirm all sounders are audible. Press "SILENCE" and "RESET" when done.
9. Turn the key switch back to the "AUTO" position. Confirm the green "SYSTEM HEALTHY" light is showing.
10. Record the test in the fire alarm test log book. Enter the date, time, name of person conducting the test, and any faults found. If no faults, write "All clear" in the remarks column.

**Section 9 – General Building Upkeep**

**9.1 External Fabric – Monthly Inspection**

Walk the full perimeter of the clubhouse and the two outbuildings (store room and pump house). Look for:

- Cracked or missing mortar between bricks.
- Loose or lifted roof tiles, particularly on the west elevation where the prevailing wind catches.
- Blocked or damaged guttering and downpipes. Clear any leaf debris by hand or with the gutter scoop. Do not use a pressure washer on the gutters; it forces water behind the fascia.
- Signage: check the main club sign and the fire exit signs are secure and legible.
- Pest entry points: any gap larger than a pencil should be reported to the committee. Do not fill gaps with expanding foam unless instructed; the building is of cavity construction and the wrong filler can bridge the damp proof course.

Report findings on the monthly walk-round sheet (kept in the maintenance office, green folder). If a defect poses an immediate safety risk, cordon off the area and contact the Facilities Manager.

**9.2 Internal Walls and Ceilings – Quarterly**

Check for:

- Damp patches or discolouration. Pay particular attention to the ceiling in the kitchen corridor and the wall behind the bar sinks. These are known problem areas.
- Loose plaster or cracked paintwork.
- Signs of water ingress around the window reveals in the main hall.

Any damp or staining must be logged. Do not paint over a damp patch without the source being identified and fixed. If the source cannot be found within the building, check the external drains on that elevation.

**9.3 Doors and Ironmongery – Quarterly**

For every internal and external door:

1. Open and close the door fully. Check it does not bind on the frame or the floor.
2. Check the hinges for loose screws. Tighten any that are loose. If a screw will not tighten, remove it, insert a wooden dowel with a little wood glue, and re-drill. This is a temporary repair; report it for a more permanent fix.
3. Check the door closer (where fitted). The door should close fully from a 30cm open position without slamming. Adjust the valve on the closer if needed. Do not over-tighten.
4. Lubricate the lock mechanism and latch with a dry PTFE spray. Do not use oil-based lubricants; they attract dust and gum up the mechanism.
5. Check the door seals and weather strips. Replace if perished.

External doors: also check the thresholds and the condition of the door itself. The main entrance door is timber and needs a coat of preservative on the bottom edge each spring.

**9.4 Windows and Ventilation – Quarterly**

- Check all window catches and stays operate correctly.
- Check the trickle vents are clear. The vents in the changing rooms block up with dust; vacuum them.
- Clean the window tracks of any debris.
- Check the sealant around the outside of the window frames is intact. Report any gaps.
- The large sliding window in the bar is on a rope and pulley system. Do not attempt to adjust the tension yourself. If it is stiff or the rope is frayed, put a note on it and report to the Facilities Manager.

**9.5 Floors and Floor Coverings – Quarterly**

**9.6 Sanitary Ware and Plumbing – Monthly**

- Check all taps for drips and correct operation. Replace washers as needed (see Section 7.2).
- Check the toilets for leaks at the base and around the cistern. Check the flush operates correctly and does not run on.
- Check the urinals in the gents. The flush timers are set to operate at peak times. Do not adjust them without authorisation.
- Check the washbasin traps for leaks. The trap under the ladies cloakroom basin is a known problem; check it every month.
- Report any limescale build-up on the shower heads in the changing rooms. The heads can be soaked in a descaler solution, but must be rinsed thoroughly before refitting.

**10. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES**

**10.1 General**

This section covers the actions to be taken in the event of an emergency affecting the club premises or its users. All staff should be familiar with the contents of this section. If in doubt, dial 999 (or 112 from a mobile) and ask for the appropriate service. Do not put yourself or others at risk.

A copy of the emergency evacuation plan is displayed in the main corridor, the kitchen, and the bar. The plan shows the assembly point, which is the far corner of the main car park, by the floodlight pole. A smaller copy is kept in the first aid room.

**10.2 Fire**

If you discover a fire:

1.  Raise the alarm by operating the nearest break-glass call point. The alarm is a continuous bell. If the bell is not heard, shout a warning to others.
2.  Call the Fire Brigade on 999. Give the address: **Meadowbank Sports Club, 14–18 Old Coach Road, Langley Green, West Sussex RH11 7QP**. Do not assume someone else has called.
3.  Attack the fire with the appropriate extinguisher **only if** the fire is small and you have been trained. Do not take risks.
4.  Leave the building by the nearest exit. Do not use the lift (there is no passenger lift). Close doors behind you.
5.  Go to the assembly point. Do not re-enter the building until told it is safe by the Fire Brigade or the Facilities Manager.

Extinguishers are located:

| Location | Type | Use on |
|---|---|---|
| Main corridor (by the office door) | Water | Paper, wood, textiles |
| Kitchen (by the exit) | CO2 | Electrical, cooking oils (small) |
| Bar (under the counter) | Foam | Flammable liquids, general |
| Boiler room (inside the door) | Powder | All types, electrical |

**Do not** use water on electrical equipment or cooking oil. If you are unsure, leave the extinguisher and get out.

**10.3 Gas Leak**

If you smell gas on the premises:

1.  Do not operate any electrical switches, including light switches. Do not use a mobile phone near the suspected leak.
2.  Open doors and windows to ventilate the area.
3.  Turn off the gas supply at the meter if it is safe to do so. The meter is located in the grey box on the external wall of the boiler room, on the car park side. The isolation valve is a lever; turn it so it is at right angles to the pipe.
4.  Leave the building and call the National Gas Emergency Service on **0800 111 999**. Give them the address and the location of the meter.
5.  Do not turn the gas back on until the leak has been located and repaired by a Gas Safe registered engineer.

**10.4 Flooding / Burst Pipe**

If water is escaping from a pipe or fitting:

1.  Turn off the water supply at the main stopcock. The stopcock is under the sink in the kitchen, behind the cleaning products. Turn it clockwise to close.
2.  Turn off the electricity supply at the consumer unit if there is any danger of water coming into contact with electrical fittings or cables. The consumer unit is in the boiler room.
3.  Contain the water if possible, using sandbags (stored in the shed), mop, and buckets. Protect the floor and any stored items.

applies to all four courts and is the current specification. No change to the surface type is
planned; any future resurfacing must use an acrylic system unless a formal variation to the
facility specification is approved by the Estates Manager.

NOTES ON SURFACE SYSTEM (ACRYLIC)
- The courts are constructed with a porous tarmacadam base (laid 1998, overlaid 2016) and a
  three-coat acrylic surfacing system.
- The acrylic system comprises a textured acrylic resurfacer, followed by two colour coats

- The system is a water-based, UV-stable acrylic. It is not suitable for use with studded
  footwear or for heavy vehicular traffic. Maintenance staff should not use metal-bladed
  scrapers on the surface.
- The expected life of the acrylic top coat is 6–8 years under normal club usage (approx.
  40 hours/week across all courts). The 2019 top coat is therefore due for renewal in the
